draft.title: Dissent in the Soviet bloc
card: The Soviet bloc was the group of Eastern European states under strong Soviet influence after 1945. Their governments were communist and followed Moscow's lead.
Dissent means open disagreement with those in power. In 1956, protests in Poland and an uprising in Hungary demanded change.
In Hungary in 1956, Soviet troops and tanks entered the country and crushed the uprising. In Czechoslovakia in 1968, the Prague Spring brought reforms that loosened government control.
The Soviet Union saw these reforms as a threat to its control. Warsaw Pact forces led by the Soviet Union invaded Czechoslovakia in 1968 and ended them.
draft.remember: Challenges to Soviet control in the bloc were put down by Soviet power.

a.q: What was the Prague Spring of 1968?
opts: A reform movement in Czechoslovakia ended by invasion
An uprising in Hungary crushed by Soviet tanks
A series of protests in Poland that won independence
A Soviet plan to reform its own government
a.why: The Prague Spring was a reform movement in Czechoslovakia, ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion. The Hungarian uprising was a different event, in 1956, and the Soviet Union did not allow independence.
a.clue: Which country, and what happened in 1968?

b.q: A student claims that Soviet leaders accepted reform in the bloc whenever it was popular. Which event from this period best shows the claim is wrong?
opts: Soviet-led forces ended Czechoslovakia's reforms in 1968
Poland held protests in 1956 that demanded change
Hungary's people supported change in 1956
Czechoslovakia's reformers were popular at home in 1968
b.why: The invasion of Czechoslovakia shows reform was stopped by force even when it was popular. The other options only show people wanted change, which does not show how Soviet leaders responded.
b.clue: Look for what the Soviet Union did, not what people wanted.

a.best: A reform movement in Czechoslovakia ended by invasion

b.best: Soviet-led forces ended Czechoslovakia's reforms in 1968

problems.detail: The remember line says challenges to Soviet control were put down by Soviet power, which covers Poland 1956. The card never says this about Poland, and it is not accurate there. The Poznań protests were suppressed by Polish forces, and the Polish October ended in a compromise with Gomułka, not a Soviet crackdown.
The clue 'Look for what the Soviet Union did' gives the answer away. Only one option describes a Soviet action, so a student can pick it without reasoning about the claim.

proposal.title: Dissent in the Soviet bloc
card: The Soviet bloc was the group of Eastern European states under strong Soviet influence after 1945. Dissent means open disagreement with those in power.
Workers' protests in Poznań were put down by Polish forces. The Soviet Union then accepted Władysław Gomułka as leader, as he kept Poland communist and loyal to Moscow.
An uprising led Hungary's new government to say it would leave the Warsaw Pact, the Soviet-led military alliance. Soviet troops and tanks crushed the uprising.
The Prague Spring brought popular reforms that loosened government control. Soviet leaders saw a threat, and Warsaw Pact forces led by the Soviet Union invaded and ended them.
proposal.remember: Soviet leaders allowed some change, but used force when reform threatened communist rule or loyalty to Moscow.

Moscow accepted Gomułka as Poland's leader in 1956

Czechoslovakia's reformers were popular at home in 1968
